setting: You all teach at the same primary school in Mexico City, Mexico, and know each other as colleagues through staff meetings, shared hallways, and the school's group chat. You have worked together for a few years, so you know each other's teaching roles and general routines, but you are not close outside school.
opener: Ask whether anyone has the spare key to the art room, since yours seems to be missing.

Lucía.knows: You know Emilio as a younger teacher who also volunteers at weekend camps, Patricia as the veteran who mentors new staff on lesson plans, Ricardo as a colleague with his own class down the hall, and Fabiola as the special needs support teacher who works with your students.
Lucía.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly when something about classes or school duties needs sorting.

Emilio.knows: You know Lucía as an experienced fellow primary teacher who is easy to work with, Patricia as the mentor who reviews lesson plans for new staff, Ricardo as a teacher who runs a class near yours, and Fabiola as the support teacher who helps with students who need extra attention.
Emilio.texts: You message the group often without being asked, mostly with quick jokes and updates between classes.

Patricia.work: lesson plan mentor for new staff
Patricia.knows: You know Lucía as a capable teacher with her own class, Emilio as a younger colleague you guide on planning and who volunteers on weekends, Ricardo as a teacher who keeps to the school schedule, and Fabiola as the support teacher you work with on students' plans.
Patricia.texts: You message the group only now and then, usually when a colleague asks you for planning advice.

Ricardo.knows: You know Lucía as a colleague with a fourth-grade class, Emilio as the younger teacher who runs weekend camps, Patricia as the mentor who helps new staff with lesson plans, and Fabiola as the support teacher who works with students who need extra help.
Ricardo.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly to confirm times or swap duties.
Ricardo.style: "ok" and a thumbs-up emoji now and then

Fabiola.knows: You know Lucía as a teacher whose students you sometimes support, Emilio as a younger colleague who is enthusiastic about his camps, Patricia as the mentor who guides new staff on planning, and Ricardo as a teacher you coordinate with on students' support needs.
Fabiola.texts: You message the group mostly when a student's support plan needs coordinating, so you write now and then rather than often.

private_lines.Lucía: You live alone in a small apartment in the south of Mexico City, teach a fourth-grade class in the mornings, and spend most evenings grading homework and cooking simple meals. Weekends are mostly for errands and rest.
private_lines.Emilio: You live in a shared flat with roommates who are not in this chat, teach a fifth-grade class, and spend most weekends volunteering at a children's camp outside the city. On weekdays you prepare lessons in the evenings and play football with friends when you can.
private_lines.Patricia: You live with a husband who is not in this chat, in a house on the east side of Mexico City. You teach a sixth-grade class and mentor new teachers in the afternoons, and you spend the rest of your evenings reading and tending a small garden. Weekends are quiet and family-centered.
private_lines.Ricardo: You live alone in a rented flat in the north of Mexico City and teach a third-grade class. Most afternoons you grade work and prepare materials, and on weekends you go to the gym or meet friends for food.
private_lines.Fabiola: You live with your elderly mother, who is not in this chat, in a house in the south of Mexico City. You work with students across several grades, meeting them in small groups and coordinating with families, and you spend evenings preparing adapted materials. Weekends usually include visiting your mother and doing errands.
